nodes.description: Prolonged action potential duration permits reactivation of L-type calcium current (and enhanced late sodium current) during phase 2/3, generating early afterdepolarizations (EADs) that trigger premature ventricular beats, especially in the setting of bradycardia and increased transmural dispersion of repolarization.

Human iPSC-derived engineered heart tissues (EHTs) with high-resolution optical mapping, exposed to the proarrhythmic perturbation used to model acquired LQTS: selective hERG blockade (E-4031) combined with hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. The model reproduces APD prolongation and tissue-scale reentry, a non-animal (NAM) system for acquired-LQTS arrhythmia mechanisms.

evidence.reference_title: Human-engineered heart tissues recapitulate tissue-scale mechanisms underlying ventricular tachycardia.
evidence.snippet: The presented platform thus provides a scalable, non-animal system for mechanistic arrhythmia research.

nodes.description: A QT-prolonging drug binds the hERG (KCNH2-encoded Kv11.1) channel and blocks the rapid delayed-rectifier potassium current IKr. hERG has an unusually large, promiscuous inner cavity, which is why chemically diverse drugs share this liability. Electrolyte disturbances such as hypokalemia further reduce IKr. This is the dominant molecular lesion of acquired LQTS.

evidence.reference_title: Drug-induced torsades de pointes: the evolving role of pharmacogenetics.
evidence.snippet: These drugs inhibit the KCNH2-encoded HERG potassium channel, which is one of the critical repolarizing forces involved in the exquisite orchestration of the heart's action potential.

evidence.reference_title: A large candidate gene survey identifies the KCNE1 D85N polymorphism as a possible modulator of drug-induced torsades de pointes.
evidence.snippet: The SNP KCNE1 D85N (rs1805128), known to modulate an important potassium current in the heart, predicted diLQTS with an odds ratio of 9.0 (95% confidence interval, 3.5-22.9).

nodes.description: Common missense modifier allele of MinK (the IKs beta-subunit), enriched in drug-induced LQTS cases over controls. A risk-modifier polymorphism rather than an ACMG-classified pathogenic variant, so clinical_significance is left unset.

evidence.snippet: Torsades de pointes (TdP) is a characteristic polymorphic ventricular arrhythmia associated with delayed ventricular repolarization as evidenced on the surface electrocardiogram by QT interval prolongation.

nodes.description: Reduced IKr diminishes the net repolarizing current during phases 2-3 of the cardiac action potential, prolonging action potential duration and the QT interval on the surface ECG. Normal repolarization is buffered by redundant potassium currents ("repolarization reserve"); when a latent genetic lesion, electrolyte disturbance, or female sex has already reduced that reserve, the same drug produces disproportionate QT prolongation.

evidence.snippet: Female sex is an independent risk factor for development of torsade de pointes (TdP) arrhythmias not only in congenital long QT syndromes but also in acquired long QT syndromes.

nodes.description: Exposure to a drug that reduces IKr/hERG -- including class IA and class III antiarrhythmics (sotalol, dofetilide, quinidine), macrolide and fluoroquinolone antibiotics, azole antifungals, antipsychotics, some antidepressants, methadone, and some antiemetics -- is the predominant cause of acquired QT prolongation. Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, and bradycardia amplify the effect.

nodes.description: EAD-triggered beats initiate a polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with a characteristic twisting QRS axis (torsades de pointes), maintained by reentry across a substrate of dispersed repolarization. It may terminate spontaneously (causing syncope) or degenerate into ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death. This tissue-level arrhythmia is the mechanistic node; the clinical finding is the Torsade de pointes phenotype.

nodes.description: A parallel molecular route to reduced IKr: rather than blocking the pore, some drugs (pentamidine, arsenic trioxide, probucol) disrupt trafficking of the hERG channel to the plasma membrane or accelerate its degradation, lowering surface channel density. The functional consequence -- reduced IKr and delayed repolarization -- converges with pore blockade. (This route reduces channel density rather than altering gating, so it is not asserted to conform to the module's gating-change trigger node; it converges on the same altered action potential downstream.)

evidence.reference_title: hERG trafficking inhibition in drug-induced lethal cardiac arrhythmia.
evidence.snippet: The mechanisms involve the disruption of hERG trafficking to the surface membrane or the acceleration of hERG protein degradation.
